questions: What is the exact definition of "odd cycle" in the context of this problem - is it a cycle with an odd number of edges, and does it include cycles of length 1 (self-loops) or length 2 (multiple edges between same vertices)?
When checking if adding an edge creates an odd cycle, do we consider only simple cycles or all possible cycles in the graph?
Is the graph guaranteed to be connected, or can it consist of multiple disconnected components?
What happens if N = 1 - can any moves be made, and who wins in this case?
When N = 2, is there always exactly one possible edge that can be added, or are there cases where no valid moves exist?
Does the "optimally" play condition require considering the entire game tree, or is there a simpler strategy that guarantees optimal play?
Are self-loops (edges from a vertex to itself) considered in the problem, and if so, how do they affect the odd cycle detection?
What is the precise tie-breaking rule when multiple valid moves are available - does the lexicographically smallest (i,j) pair have any special significance?

inline_prompts: You are given a simple undirected graph with N vertices and M edges, with vertices labeled 1 to N and edges labeled 1 to M. The i-th edge connects vertices U_i and V_i. Initially, G does not contain an odd cycle. A sequence of vertices (v₀, v₁, …, vₖ) forms an odd cycle if and only if: • k is odd, • v₀ = vₖ, and • every consecutive pair (vᵢ₋₁, vᵢ) is connected by an edge in G. Takahashi and Aoki will play a game using this graph G. With Aoki going first, they take turns performing the following operation: - Choose a pair of integers (i,j) with 1 ≤ i < j ≤ N that satisfies both of the following conditions, then add an edge connecting vertices i and j to G. - G does not already have an edge connecting vertices i and j. - Adding an edge connecting vertices i and j does not create an odd cycle. A player who cannot perform this operation loses, and the other player wins. Determine who wins when both players play optimally. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N M U_1 V_1 U_2 V_2 \vdots U_M V_M Output If Aoki (the first player) wins, print Aoki; otherwise, if Takahashi (the second player) wins, print Takahashi. Constraints - 1 ≤ N ≤ 2×10^5 - 0 ≤ M ≤ 2×10^5 - 1 ≤ U_i < V_i ≤ N - The given graph does not contain an odd cycle. - The given graph does not contain multi-edges. - All input values are integers.
